messages:
maria-cs: Heads up — customer reported intermittent 403s during their nightly batch embedding job. Single-item embeddings work fine, but batched requests (50+ inputs) get a 403: "insufficient_scope: missing embeddings.create and inference.generate". They say key was provisioned via SSO the same morning.

alex-support: Can you paste a minimal repro + key id (last 8) and whether this is a service account or user key? Also which region/org.

maria-cs: Repro steps from customer (sanitized):
1) POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings
2) Authorization: Bearer sk-XXXX...abcd (svcacct)
3) Body: { "model": "open-embed-xl", "inputs": ["...", "...", ... ~60 items] }

Error log snippet:
```
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
content-type: application/json
{
  "error": {
    "code": 403,
    "message": "insufficient_scope: required scopes [embeddings.create inference.generate rerank.create]",
    "status": "PERMISSION_DENIED"
  }
}
```
Key last8: abcd1234, org: acme-inc, region: us-west-2

sam-eng: Thanks. This smells like a provisioning mismatch — sometimes the SSO/provisioner runs in dry-run and never applies non-core scopes. Can you confirm by hitting the admin listing for the key? Example:
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \n  https://api.redwood.ai/admin/keys/abcd1234
```
Look for the `scopes` array in the response; if embeddings/rerank/inference are absent that explains it.

eve-identity: Confirmed — I pulled the admin record for abcd1234. Response shows:
```
{ "id": "abcd1234", "owner_org": "acme-inc", "scopes": [ "billing.read", "usage.read" ], "created_by": "sso-provisioner:v2-dryrun" }
```
Provisioner v2 introduced a flag where non-core scopes were gated behind an allowlist that was accidentally empty in dry-run mode. We pushed a fix 12:10 UTC but any keys created during the window need remediation.

eve-identity: Quick remediation options (pick one):
- Manual patch (fastest): POST /admin/keys/abcd1234/scopes with body ["inference.generate","embeddings.create","rerank.create"] to add scopes.
- Rotate: create a new svcacct key via admin API with the correct scopes and rotate in customer's system (recommended for audit clarity).

ops-bot: remediation-job queued -> job_id=j-20220322-77, task=apply_scopes, target_key=abcd1234, requested_scopes=3

sam-eng: Follow-ups:
- I'll open a pipeline PR to add a post-provisioning check that calls the admin API and fails if required scopes are missing (preventive).
- For this customer, manual patch + rotate is safest: patch to restore immediate function, then issue new key and rotate within 24h.

maria-cs: Thanks team. I'll notify the customer (high priority), offer to create a temporary key for their batch run, and schedule rotation. @sam-eng @eve-identity please keep me posted when remediation job completes so I can close the loop with account.

sam-eng: Will monitor the job. If you see any residual 403s after the scope add, collect a failed request id and send logs — might be a cache TTL on authorization that we need to invalidate.

eve-identity: Note for postmortem: add a telemetry alert when provisioner publishes keys with source tag containing "dryrun" or when created_by contains unknown agent. That would have flagged this automatically.

maria-cs: Ack. Customer notified, they accepted temp key. Marking as escalated -> SVC-PRIORITY high. Will update thread after rotation.
